pull_request.title: Remove unused benchmark inputs and temporary scan buffers
pull_request.body:
Mixed workloads previously constructed values for reads and deletes, then discarded those values inside the measured interval; scans retained an entirely unused batch. Prepare only the keys, values or bounds each operation consumes, and share the unchanged target-ID schedule between preparation and model updates.

Matrix scans now append borrowed keys directly into one output buffer for both engines, removing temporary per-key vectors while preserving lazy value loading. This PR is stacked on #7 and contains only benchmark changes and their notes; merge #7 first, then retarget this PR to main.

Validation: native all-target/Wasm benchmark Clippy, the host protocol test, formatting, documentation links and dependency checks pass. Both benchmark suites pass 2,280 measurements with exact repeats, matching model/results and unchanged stable capacities. Heap capacities change. The engine-only baseline rebuild is byte-identical across worktrees. Full local release CI was not run.

All 46 matrix key-scan cases improve for both engines; our reductions range from 12.9% to 86.0%. These fixture changes establish a new baseline rather than an algorithm speedup: our mixed row/index totals increase 0.9300%/0.0887%, and one mixed row scan increases 87.9389%. Upstream mixed rows increase 1.0231% and indexes decrease 0.0905%. The full comparison and artifact identities are recorded in docs/design/canonical-workloads.md under Benchmark input and key projection cleanup.

Pending notes remain 0.4.1. Package versions, dependency selections, wire IDs and CSV labels are unchanged.

issue.title: Reuse decoded children during B-tree deletion

repository.name: ic-storage
repository.description: Governed stable collections for Internet Computer applications using IC Memory allocation handles.

issue.body:
Deletion decoded a child during balancing and decoded it again during recursion; merging also reread both siblings. Carry the validated Node values through preparation, merging and recursive deletion instead. This avoids stable reads and staged-page decoding while preserving comparator/payload checks, reclamation order and unpublished failed mutations.

An explicit duplicate-sibling guard preserves a corruption refusal previously supplied by rereading a page just staged free. The new regression reproduces the previous refusal, catches the unguarded prototype and verifies refusal without writes. Read budgets improve from three to two for ordinary descent and five to three for merging deletion/root collapse and the balancing miss.

This PR is stacked on #8: merge the cleanup PRs first, then retarget this PR to main. The benchmark fixture and dependency graph remain unchanged. No public API, persisted format or package version changes; pending notes remain 0.4.1.

Validation: 40 regular library tests, three adapter tests, eight Rustdoc examples, native/Wasm Clippy, formatting, documentation links and dependency checks pass. Three deletion regressions pass on Rust 1.91. The selected build passes the 320,000-operation differential campaign against upstream and the independent model. Full local release CI was not run.

With a byte-identical baseline, both benchmark suites pass 2,280 measurements with exact repeats and unchanged capacities/results. Mixed row instructions decrease 0.9946%, indexes 2.0800%. All 46 matrix removal cases improve (up to 13.34%); the other 460 cases and upstream counts are unchanged. Mixed sequences remain uneven: 14 of 64 cases increase, including one row key scan at +50.52%. The cause of those individual allocation/compiler shifts is not isolated. Full results and retained artifact identities are in docs/design/canonical-workloads.md under Reuse decoded nodes during deletion.

+
+## Benchmark input and key projection cleanup
+
+The next 0.4.1 change is confined to the non-published benchmark. Reads/deletes
+prepare keys without unused values; scans prepare bounds without an unused
+32-record batch. Writes prepare keys and values, and one target-ID helper owns
+the unchanged permutation/miss schedule for preparation and model updates.
+Matrix key scans append borrowed slices directly into their output buffer,
+removing temporary per-key vectors in both engines. Key-only scans still never
+load value payloads. Wire IDs, operation order, CSV labels and model data remain
+unchanged. The measurement fixture and allocation histories deliberately change.
+
+Native all-target and Wasm benchmark Clippy and the host protocol test pass.
+The final canister passes all 2,024 matrix and 256 mixed measurements, with exact
+repeats, matching result sizes/model checks and unchanged stable capacities.
+Heap capacities differ from the engine-only build. A rebuild of the engine-only
+source in the second worktree reproduces its Wasm bytes exactly, establishing
+the comparison anchor. All builds use the same lockfile, runner and toolchain
+identities as the preceding node-reclamation qualification.
+
+| Engine / mixed workload | Engine-only baseline | New fixture | Change |
+| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
+| Ours / rows | 314,042,756 | 316,963,272 | +0.9300% |
+| Ours / index | 186,970,602 | 187,136,538 | +0.0887% |
+| Upstream / rows | 341,486,075 | 344,979,980 | +1.0231% |
+| Upstream / index | 114,279,492 | 114,176,042 | -0.0905% |
+
+All 46 matrix key-scan cases improve for each engine: our reductions range from
+12.8941% to 86.0365%, and upstream reductions from 0.4308% to 85.4517%. Across
+our complete 506-case matrix, 368 improve, 92 are unchanged and 46 increase,
+by at most 0.0187%. Wins against upstream remain 381/506.
+
+Mixed costs move in both directions: our largest decrease is 14.0497% for row
+values_forward_0; the largest increase is 87.9389% for row keys_forward_1.
+Removing unused inputs changes allocation/drop history outside and inside
+measurement windows. These are new benchmark-fixture baselines, not storage
+algorithm speedups or an isolation of the allocator/compiler cause. Keep them
+separate from the preceding engine-only comparison. Actual IcyDB codecs,
+recovery, macOS and full local release CI remain outside this qualification.
+
+The same `target/reclamation-benchmark.sjh5wqb7/` attempt retains the final build
+under `final/`, with runner, Wasm, lockfile and both CSV/log suites;
+`engine-to-final.csv` and `.json` retain comparisons. Final Wasm SHA-256:
+`2b7e204c3d743fcea60ae571ed2558cd361dfd221038a607921887d4016de325`.
